question: What colour is denim yarn at the moment it comes out of the indigo dye bath?
answer: Yellowish green. Indigo will not dissolve in water, so dyers chemically reduce it to leuco-indigo, a soluble pale yellow-green form that soaks into cotton. Lifted into the air, the yarn oxidises to blue within a minute or two, locking the dye in. Mills send it up over rollers between dips for air.
move: Some finished colours exist only after the air has had its turn.
ask: What in my life only shows its true colour after some time has passed?
reference: Jenny Balfour-Paul, Indigo: Egyptian Mummies to Blue Jeans, British Museum Press, 2011
